# `in` standard library

`in` provides a shared buffered reader over standard input. Read operations
return an optional ram: the positive slot carries data, and the unit second
slot indicates EOF or would-block / error status. Status accessors expose the
underlying reader state.

| Function | Result | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `read_line(max)` | `< String | >` | read through newline; remove trailing carriage return |
| `read_bytes(max)` | `< String | >` | read at most `max` available bytes |
| `read_byte!` | `< Int | >` | read one byte |
| `read_until(delim, max)` | `< String | >` | read through and consume `delim` |
| `err!` | `Int` | returns last errno encountered (0 if none) |
| `eof!` | `<>` | true (`<+>`) if clean EOF has been reached on stdin |
| `would_block!` | `<>` | true (`<+>`) if the last read on stdin encountered `EAGAIN` / `EWOULDBLOCK` |
| `has_err!` | `<>` | true (`<+>`) if an unhandled I/O error occurred (`err != 0`) |
| `clear!` | `()` | clears the error and EOF flags on the stdin reader |

```{.dva .partial reason="reads from interactive stdin"}
#use in
#use io

line = in::read_line(4096)
line | text => io::out(text) | io::out("end of input")
```

The reader is module-global, so calls share buffering and advance the same
standard-input stream. Use `io::reader(fd)` directly when a program needs a
separate reader or a descriptor other than standard input.
